title: Using Microfluidics Chips for Live Imaging and Study of Injury Responses in Drosophila Larvae
protocol: Mix 45 g of PDMS base and 4.5 g of curing agent in a small disposable plastic container.
Place the mixture in a vacuum container for 10 minutes to remove bubbles.
Place the SU-8 mold at the bottom of a 150 mm diameter plastic dish.
Slowly pour the degassed PDMS mixture onto the SU-8 mold, avoiding bubble formation.
Cure the PDMS in an oven at 650 °C for 4 hours.
Remove the cured PDMS/SU-8 mold from the oven and allow it to cool.
Cut the cured PDMS along the edge of the SU-8 mold using a razor blade.
Divide the PDMS slab into individual chips using a razor blade.
Poke a hole in the vacuum port of each PDMS chip with a 21 G dispensing needle.
Twist a 23 G dispensing needle from its base to break off the tip.
Insert the 23 G needle tip into a small piece of polyethylene tubing.
Cut excess tubing away from the needle with a razor blade.
Create a plastic ring around one end of the needle for sealing purposes.
For inverted microscope use: insert the 23 G needle tip directly into the vacuum port hole.
For upright microscope use: poke an additional side hole on the PDMS chip with a 21 G dispensing needle.
Insert the 23 G needle tip, including tubing ring, into the side hole of the PDMS chip.
Place double-sided tape over the top of the PDMS chip to seal the top hole.
Take a piece of polyethylene tubing approximately 20 cm in length.
Connect one end of the tubing to the needle tip inserted into the vacuum port.
Attach the other end of the tubing to a port on a 3-way valve.
Connect a 20 ml syringe to one remaining port of the 3-way valve.
Leave the last port of the 3-way valve open to the environment.
Clean the PDMS chip with transparent adhesive tape.
Attach a piece of tape to the bottom surface of the PDMS chip.
Ensure the tape touches the entire PDMS surface.
Peel off the tape after attachment.
Repeat steps 2-3 times to ensure no particles or oil remain on the PDMS chip surface.
Transfer early (foraging) 3rd instar larvae to a Petri dish containing water.
Bathe the larvae in water to remove culture medium.
Place a small drop of Halocarbon 700 oil at the center of a clean glass coverslip.
Gently pick up an early-staged 3rd instar larva from the water using forceps.
Briefly place the larva on a lightweight wipe or paper towel to remove excess water.
Place the larva on the oil drop, ensuring trachea are not coated.
Let the larva remain on the oil drop for 10 seconds.
Remove the larva from the oil drop and place it on another clean glass coverslip.
Transfer the larva to a final clean glass coverslip to remove excess oil.
Ensure proper orientation of the larva for imaging, with the ventral side facing the coverslip.
Gently place the PDMS chip on top of the larva.
Align the larva to the center middle of the microchamber with its tail oriented towards the vacuum port.
Push the PDMS chip against the glass coverslip to achieve a good seal.
Ensure that the larva is entirely enclosed by the microchamber when the PDMS chip touches the glass coverslip.
Switch the 3-way valve such that the syringe can draw air from the PDMS microchamber through the tubing.
Hold the PDMS chip/glass coverslip firmly with one hand.
Pull the syringe plunger with the other hand to withdraw 2-2.5 ml of air until resistance is felt in the syringe handle.
Switch the valve off such that the PDMS chip is isolated from the syringe and from the environment.
Check the larva under the stereoscope.
Ensure that the entire animal body is placed inside the microchamber.
Verify that the animal is immobile.
Observe that the trachea is visible.
Confirm that the rest of the PDMS chip is in contact with the coverslip.
Handle the larva chip (PDMS chip + glass coverslip) carefully to avoid detachment.
Fix the 'top' side of the chip to the microscope stage with double-sided tape for an upright microscope.
Use a high-magnification objective (oil-immersion, 40-63X recommended) to locate the animal's structure(s) of interest and perform imaging.
Switch to lower magnification if needed to identify the desired region for imaging before switching to higher magnification.
Release the vacuum by switching the valve to an open position after imaging is completed.
Detach the PDMS chip from the coverslip carefully.
Remove the larva immediately with forceps.
Place the larva gently on a grape-juice agar plate for recovery.
Isolate early staged 3rd instar larvae of the desired genotype.
Bathe the larvae in water to remove food.
Subdue larvae using a standard fly CO2 anesthetization station with CO2 pad under a dissection stereomicroscope.
Place a single anesthetized larva onto a grape juice agar plate under the stereomicroscope.
Turn the animal ventral side up to visualize the ventral nerve cord and segmental nerves through the cuticle.
Pinch the segmental nerves tightly through the cuticle for 5-10 seconds using Dumostar number-5 forceps.
After the injury, turn the animal so that its ventral side down on the grape plate.
Ensure the animal can move its head and eat.
Keep injured animals on the grape juice agar plate at 25°C for the desired time according to the experimental objective.
